items.title: The MCP Tasks Extension
items.author: AAIF Live
items.summary:
Orchestrating Agent Swarms with MCP and Sandboxes

What happens when you move beyond a single AI agent and start coordinating entire swarms of agents?

In this session, Vikram Vaswani, Developer Advocate at Melonfire, explores how MCP can be used to orchestrate multi-agent systems alongside sandboxes, durable workflows, and observability.

Vikram dives into the practical architecture behind coordinating agent swarms, showing how MCP can help agents interact with tools and shared environments while sandboxes provide the isolation needed to run these workflows safely. The session also explores how open-source tooling, durable execution, and observability can make increasingly complex agent systems easier to manage and operate.

Whether you're experimenting with multi-agent architectures or looking at how to build more reliable agentic workflows, this session offers practical ideas for orchestrating agents beyond the single-agent model.

🎤 Speaker: Vikram Vaswani - Developer Advocate, Melonfire
📌 Topic: Orchestrating Agent Swarms with MCP and Sandboxes

items.title: Agentic DX: Bringing IDP into your IDE
items.author: AAIF Live
items.summary:
Agentic DX: Bringing IDP into Your IDE

How do you get developers to actually adopt an Internal Developer Platform when onboarding feels like one more thing standing between them and shipping?

In this session, Adnan Vahora, Software Engineer at Motorola Solutions, shares how his team tackled this challenge with an IDP serving 4,000+ monthly active users by bringing the platform directly into the developer’s IDE through a “Bring Your Own Agent” approach.

Adnan explores what happened when they started building a composable agent framework, and the hard lessons that followed. From the limitations of flat agent meshes and hallucinations snowballing across agents to the often-overlooked boundary between MCP and A2A, the talk dives into where agentic systems can break down in practice.

The session introduces a Master Agent architecture and a practical approach to maintaining “Agentic Context Hygiene”, offering developers and platform teams a blueprint for building more reliable agent-driven developer experiences.

🎤 Speaker: Adnan Vahora - Software Engineer, Motorola Solutions
📌 Topic: Agentic DX: Bringing IDP into Your IDE

items.title: Responsible Autonomy: Building Governance Frameworks for AI That Act in the Real World via MCP
items.author: AAIF Live
items.summary:
Responsible Autonomy: Building Governance Frameworks for AI Agents That Act in the Real World via MCP

What happens when AI agents move beyond answering questions and start taking real-world actions?

In this session, Saurabh Mishra, Lead DevOps Engineer at Optum, explores the governance challenges that emerge as MCP-powered agents gain the ability to read emails, update CRMs, execute code, move money, and trigger business workflows autonomously.

Rather than focusing solely on what agents can do, Saurabh looks at how organizations can deploy them responsibly without sacrificing the speed and autonomy that make agentic AI valuable.

Drawing on real-world examples across finance, healthcare, legal, and enterprise IT, the session introduces practical approaches for implementing scoped permissions, human-in-the-loop controls, audit trails, and policy guardrails for MCP-connected agents.

If you're building or deploying AI agents that can take action in real-world systems, this session offers a practical framework for answering one of the most important questions in agentic AI: who is accountable when an agent acts?

🎤 Speaker: Saurabh Mishra - Lead DevOps Engineer, Optum
📌 Topic: Responsible Autonomy: Building Governance Frameworks for AI Agents That Act in the Real World via MCP

items.title: MCP 728: What Changes, What Breaks, and What You Need to Do About It
items.author: AAIF Live
items.summary:
MCP 728: What Changes, What Breaks, and What You Need to Do About It

The MCP 728 specification introduces some of the biggest changes yet to the Model Context Protocol — and teams building with MCP need to understand what’s changing and how to prepare.

In this session, Mateo Torres, Developer Advocate at Arcade.dev, breaks down the new specification and what it means for developers and organizations already building or deploying MCP.

The 728 spec removes the session handshake, formalizes servers as OAuth 2.1 resource servers, makes extensions first-class, and deprecates features including Sampling and Roots. These changes also kick off a 12-month migration clock, giving teams a limited window to adapt their existing implementations.

Mateo explores both the tactical and strategic decisions teams will need to make — from re-architecting authentication to deciding whether to support both protocol versions or introduce a runtime layer in front of MCP.

If you're building, operating, or planning to adopt MCP, this session offers a practical guide to what changes, what might break, and what you should be doing now.

🎤 Speaker: Mateo Torres — Developer Advocate, Arcade.dev
📌 Topic: MCP 728: What Changes, What Breaks, and What You Need to Do About It

items.title: What We Learned from Dozens of Enterprise MCP Deployments
items.author: AAIF Live
items.summary:
What We Learned from Dozens of Enterprise MCP Deployments

What does it actually take to run MCP in production at enterprise scale?

In this session, Jiquan Ngiam, Co-Founder & CEO of MintMCP, shares lessons gathered from working with dozens of enterprise teams deploying the Model Context Protocol in real-world environments.

Rather than focusing on a single deployment, Jiquan breaks down the recurring patterns, challenges, and architectural decisions that emerged across different enterprise environments, from where teams commonly got stuck to what held up as MCP adoption expanded.

The session explores practical considerations around authentication, agent identity, tool management, observability, policy enforcement, and operating MCP at scale, offering a grounded look at what it takes to move from experimenting with MCP to running it reliably in production.

Whether you're evaluating MCP for your organization or already deploying it across enterprise workflows, this session offers practical lessons and hard-earned insights from the field.

Speaker: Jiquan Ngiam - Co-Founder & CEO, MintMCP
Topic: What We Learned from Dozens of Enterprise MCP Deployments
